content: Interventions for the management of submucous cleft palate include a variety of surgical and non-surgical approaches aimed at addressing the functional and anatomical deficits associated with this condition. Surgical techniques are often employed to correct the underlying structural abnormalities of the soft palate, such as the repair of the levator veli palatini muscle to restore proper velopharyngeal function. This may involve procedures like intravelar veloplasty or pharyngeal flap surgery, depending on the severity of the velopharyngeal insufficiency. Non-surgical management may include speech therapy to address compensatory articulation errors and improve resonance disorders. In some cases, prosthetic devices such as palatal obturators or speech bulbs may be utilized to temporarily improve velopharyngeal closure, particularly in patients who are not candidates for surgery or are awaiting surgical intervention. The choice of intervention is typically guided by a multidisciplinary team, including surgeons, speech-language pathologists, and other specialists, who assess the patient's specific anatomical and functional needs. Postoperative care and long-term follow-up are essential to monitor speech outcomes, velopharyngeal function, and overall quality of life.
